production.note: Calendar build years; never sold new in the US. Start: Toyota's 75-years history page gives a release date of 1994/2/2 and notes 2,100 units released in February 1994 for the Japanese market (the WRC homologation run); PistonHeads: Toyota 'launched the ST205 generation of GT-Four in the UK, in May 1994' (pistonheads-st205). End: Garage Dreams gives 'Year of production ... 1994 - 1999' (garagedreams-st205); no Toyota page stating the end date was opened.

body.note: Two-door liftback coupe; inferred from the cited pages' description and photographs.

configuration.note: 'The Celica's 2.0-litre four-cylinder twin-cam 16 valve engine was substantially modified' (3S-GTE; engine code per toyota-75years-gt-four)

aspiration.note: Single turbo: the engine was modified with 'a larger, water intercooled turbocharger'.

drivetrain.note: 'With permanent four-wheel drive' (Toyota GB); a permanent system, so AWD.

transmission.note: PistonHeads spec table: 'Five-speed manual'; 'The E154 five-speed manual transmission in the Celica is tough.' Garage Dreams agrees ('5-speed manual E154F', garagedreams-st205). No Toyota page naming the gearbox was opened.

powerHp.note: Japanese-market rating. Quote (Toyota 75-years spec table, GT-FOUR column): "-/255/6000", with the footnote that the slash-separated figures are kW, PS and r.p.m., i.e. 255 PS at 6,000 rpm. 255 PS x 0.98632 = 251.5, rounded to 252 hp. Garage Dreams agrees: '252 horsepower for the Japanese market' (garagedreams-st205). Export cars were rated lower: Toyota GB quotes 239 bhp (toyota-uk-gt-four-history).

weightLb.note: Japanese-market GT-Four, 5-speed manual. Quote: curb mass '1380' kg. 1,380 kg x 2.20462 = 3,042.4, rounded to 3,042 lb. The spec column is model code E-ST205-BLMVZ on a page whose release note describes the February 1994 Japanese launch. See discrepancies for Garage Dreams' 1,390 kg.

discrepancies.reason: Toyota's 75-years table gives 1,380 kg (3,042 lb); Garage Dreams gives '1390 kg (3064 lbs)'. 10 kg apart (0.7%), possibly standard GT-Four versus the February 1994 WRC homologation version, or rounding.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Toyota's own 1,380 kg figure (weight order step 1); the manufacturer figure outranks the enthusiast site.
